analysis.title: Buckling up
key_insights: Markets face a heavy week: FOMC meeting, PCE data, month-end Treasury auctions and month-end index extension trade.

House view is that the FOMC holds rates this week and hikes in December. The report says this is in line with market pricing, which prices little chance of a hike this week and around 22bp of tightening by year-end.

AI jitters and volatility in euro-area government bonds created haven demand for Treasuries, taking the 10Y Treasury yield back to 5.00%, 30bp below the early-October peak and right on its 50-day moving average. A rally in energy markets pushed yields modestly higher last Friday.

Stronger-than-expected September inflation data makes the October FOMC meeting more interesting despite the expected hold. Economists forecast core PCE tracking firmly in September, with MoM near the rounding cusp between 0.3% and 0.4% and YoY rising to 3.1% from 3.0%.
Core FOMC members have suggested a bias towards holding in October.
Coupon supply is heavy this week: USD69bn 2Y auction Monday, USD70bn 5Y Tuesday and USD44bn 7Y Thursday. Month-end extension is a focus on Friday.
The desk favours curve flatteners. With little Fed action expected near term the front end is anchored, and flight-to-quality trades would benefit the long end.
Relative value: the desk likes being long 10Y vs 5Y and 30Y because the 10Y looks cheap.

Base case for mid-term elections is that Democrats regain the House, producing legislative gridlock whichever party controls the Senate. A divided government would reduce the odds of major spending programmes and tax cuts, easing upward pressure on Treasury term premium and long-term yields. This would support lower long-end yields and a flatter curve.
